In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the finite element method is a viable and effective method for solving the peridynamic evolution equations.

for the peridynamic evolution problem with nonlocal nonlinearity, the time discretization error dominates the spatial error for $\Delta t$ of $O(1)$ and the time discretization scheme must be stable in the mean square sense for any given $\Delta t$.

for a finite element discretization of the nonlocal equation of motion the rate of convergence to the actual solution is $C_t\epsilon^{-2} h^{2} \Delta t$ where $h,\Delta t$ are the mesh size and time step respectively and $\epsilon$ is a parameter that characterizes the nonlocality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rate of convergence is independent of the time step and the mesh size.

for the time stepping scheme we obtain the rate of convergence $C_t \Delta t + C_s h^2 / \epsilon^2$, while for the space discretization we obtain the rate $C_2 h^2/\Delta t$ and $C_1 h^2/\sqrt{\epsilon}$.
we have established the rate of convergence for the finite element method applied to the nonlocal peridynamic equations and have developed the energy stability for the time stepping scheme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
for nonlocal models the rate of convergence is determined by $\epsilon$ rather than $h$ and $\Delta t$.
